original_target.title: Does local stability imply global attraction for Nicholson’s blowflies equation?

problem_statement: For $`p>1`$ and $`\tau>0`$ consider $`x'(t)=-x(t)+p\,x(t-\tau)e^{-x(t-\tau)}`$ with arbitrary continuous history $`x(s)>0`$ on $`[-\tau,0]`$. The positive equilibrium is $`x_* =\log p`$. Suppose every root of $`z+1-(1-\log p)e^{-z\tau}=0`$ has strictly negative real part, so the equilibrium is locally exponentially stable. Must every such positive solution satisfy $`x(t)\to\log p`$ as $`t\to\infty`$? Parameter values with imaginary characteristic roots are excluded from the premise.
recommendation: Retain Open; bounded searches found no full match, not a certification of openness.
scope_comparison: All p>1, tau>0 satisfying strict characteristic-root stability; all continuous strictly positive histories; eventual convergence to log p. Recent diffusive/viscous or mortality-delay models and sufficient delay conditions do not imply the full local-to-global statement.
